model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net_debt = 0

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Book value per common share CAGR normalised for the Schwab gain: FY2022 55.00 -> FY2025 68.78 is 7.7% (TD_Annual_FY2022_MDA.txt:100; TD_Annual_FY2025_MDA.txt:128), but FY2025 BVPS carries ~C$5/share of the one-time C$8.6B Schwab gain; ex-gain (~63.7) the 3yr CAGR is ~5.0% and the 5yr (FY2020 49.49, TD_Annual_FY2021_MDA.txt:108) ~5.2%. 5.0% is the forward base year-1 revenue growth; the 7-10% FY2029 EPS objective sits above it because EPS growth also carries the buyback (~3.5%/yr at C$10B on a C$275B market cap).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr adjusted-revenue CAGR 10.2% exceeds the 3yr BVPS CAGR 7.7% by ~32% and the 3yr adjusted-EPS CAGR is 0.0% (FY2022 8.36 -> FY2025 8.37): FY2022 was TD's pre-AML peak (adjusted ROE 15.9%) and FY2023-25 absorbed the Global Resolution, the US balance-sheet restructuring, the loss of Schwab equity income and ~US$500M/yr of remediation spend while revenue grew. The three rates disagree because the last three years are a reset, not a trend; the forward base path (5% -> 3%) is set below every historical revenue rate and the margin path, not growth, carries the recovery.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on ADJUSTED total revenue (FY2020 42,225; FY2022 46,170; FY2025 61,810) -- reported FY2025 revenue 67,777 includes the C$8,975M Schwab gain. EPS CAGRs are on ADJUSTED diluted EPS (FY2020 5.36; FY2022 8.36; FY2025 8.37); reported EPS (6.43 / 9.47 / 11.56) is distorted by the FY2020 Ameritrade gain and the FY2025 Schwab gain. fcf_*_cagr fields carry ADJUSTED NET INCOME TO COMMON CAGRs (FY2020 9,701; FY2022 15,166; FY2025 14,460; TTM 16,372): bank OCF/FCF swings with trading assets, deposits and securities and is not an owner cash flow. 9M-FY26 adjusted EPS 7.59 is +23% YoY (easy comparison) and adjusted NI to common +18%.

scenario_narratives.base: TD executes the September-2025 Investor Day plan roughly on schedule: the Canadian P&C and Wealth franchises compound at mid-single digits, Wholesale (TD Securities/TD Cowen) normalises from a record year, US Banking grows modestly inside the US$434B cap and lifts its ROE from ~10% as the balance-sheet restructuring drag annualises away, the C$825M restructuring programme and the fading of US$550M/yr remediation spend after the calendar-2027 lookback take efficiency to the mid-50s by FY2029, and PCL settles at ~0.45% of loans. Revenue growth 5% fading to 3%, adjusted ROE ~15% rising to ~16-17%, CET1 run at ~13% with the surplus returned through the C$10B NCIB and a dividend at a 40-50% payout. The asset cap is NOT assumed to lift inside the explicit horizon; its lift is upside to this case.
scenario_narratives.bull: The remediation lands cleanly: the SAR lookback completes in 2027, the monitor and the OCC validate the programme and the asset cap lifts in 2028, releasing ~US$52B of headroom plus uncapped growth in a Maine-to-Florida franchise that has been shrinking for three years. Remediation spend (~C$750M/yr) falls away, AI/branch-format productivity takes efficiency to ~52-53%, credit stays benign at ~0.38%, and TD closes the ROE gap to RY (19-20%). Revenue 7% fading to 3.5%; terminal multiple 14x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: The remediation timeline extends beyond 2027 after additional findings widen the lookback; the asset cap persists into 2029 or later, the OCC imposes the further 7% US asset reduction, and remediation/monitorship costs stay elevated so the efficiency target slips. On top of that the CUSMA review fails or broad US tariffs return and Canada enters recession in FY2028 with PCL at ~0.80% of loans and revenue down 2%. No solvency or funding case (CET1 14.3%, TLAC 31.1%), but earnings power resets to a ~30% pre-tax margin and the market re-rates TD from 17x adjusted earnings back to a discounted Big Six multiple (10x FCFE).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what common shareholders can take out: adjusted net income to common less the earnings that must be retained to hold CET1 at ~13% as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the CAD cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are operating funding, so there is no net-debt deduction; preferred/AT1 distributions are removed inside the flow. The base is TTM ADJUSTED earnings to 2026-07-31, which excludes the one-time C$8.6B Schwab gain and the balance-sheet-restructuring losses but keeps the ~US$550M/yr AML remediation spend and the asset-cap NII drag as real costs of doing business until they roll off. Flows and the bridge are in CAD; the per-share result is converted to USD at 0.7019 for comparison with the NYSE quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Remediation timeline: the SAR lookback and monitor/regulator validation decide when the asset cap lifts; the base case assumes remediation spend fades after calendar 2027 but does NOT assume the cap lifts inside the horizon. An extension costs margin (bear), a clean 2028 lift adds US growth (bull).
Credit cycle: PCL is 6.0% of revenue at 0.40% of loans, at the low end of the 40-50bp guidance; a 0.80% year takes ~C$4B pre-tax out of one year's earnings and the model assumes it does not recur.
Fee-cycle peak: Wholesale Banking (+25% revenue YoY, +87% net income) and Wealth (AUM +23%) made FY2026 a record; a reversal hits year-1 growth and margin directly.

Adjusted vs reported: the model uses adjusted earnings; restructuring (C$686M FY25, C$200M 9M-FY26) and the FHN hedge unwind (C$205M/yr) are excluded as items of note but have recurred for three years. If restructuring is a permanent feature the margin path is ~0.3pt too high.

Capital run-rate: retention is set for 13.0% CET1 and the ~130bp surplus (~US$3.6/share) is not credited; if OSFI, the OCC or the DOJ plea agreement pin more capital inside the group, FCFE falls one-for-one and the surplus never reaches shareholders.
FX: the CAD->USD conversion at 0.7019 moves the USD value one-for-one; ~40% of earnings are USD-denominated, which partly hedges the translation.
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 13x FCFE cap (vs a 15.3x Gordon multiple at 9.75%/3%) and 3% CAD nominal terminal growth drive it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE TD, USD); TSX TD.TO and CADUSD=X fetched for the parity check; 52-week range 77.95-125.47 USD
data_sources.financials: TD Q3-2026 Report to Shareholders (Aug 27, 2026; Table 1 highlights, shares, CET1 14.3%, RWA 653.4B; Table 2/3 reported and adjusted results incl. NI to common adjusted and items of note; Table 6 average common equity 113,810; Note 12 share capital 1,638,511 thousand common shares, preferred and other equity 12,829; Note 13 stock-option expense; cash flow statement buybacks C$2,394M quarter / C$7,445M 9M; AML remediation update and US$550M guidance); FY2025 Annual Report MD&A (Table 1 and Table 3 adjusted results, BVPS 68.78, adjusted ETR 21.3%, Q4-25 adjusted NIE 8,540 and NI 3,905) and Financial Statements (Note 21 stock-option expense C$22.9M; cash flow buybacks 6,206 and dividends 7,663); FY2021/FY2022 Annual MD&A for FY2020/FY2022 adjusted EPS, adjusted NI to common, adjusted revenue and BVPS; TD_Metrics.csv / TD.duckdb kpis for revenue, NI, EPS, dividends, PreferredEquity and TotalCommonEquity history.
data_sources.qualitative: TD_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Oct-2024 Global Resolution (US$3.09B penalties, guilty pleas, US$434B asset cap, monitorship), Feb-2025 Schwab exit (C$21.0B proceeds, C$8.6B net gain, +238bp CET1), US balance-sheet restructuring (US$382B vs cap), Sept-2025 Investor Day targets (FY26 ~13% ROE / 6-8% EPS growth; FY29 ~16% ROE / 7-10% EPS growth, mid-50s efficiency, 40-50% payout), C$10B NCIB announced 2026-09-30, CUSMA/tariff and FINTRAC risk framing.

inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled share-based compensation is the stock-option expense only: C$22.9M FY2025 (FY2024 C$34.2M; TD_Annual_FY2025_FinancialStatements.txt:2840, Note 21) and C$25.7M for 9M-FY2026 (TD_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:3895, Note 13); TTM taken as ~C$30M. The Metrics.csv StockBasedComp series (C$1,043M FY2025) is total share-based compensation including cash-settled share units, which are inside adjusted non-interest expense and hedged, so they are already charged in the flow and must not be deducted again. Options potentially exercisable 6.2M (Q3-26 Note, line 3971).
inputs.fx_note: CAD->USD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-04T04:21Z), the same rate used for RY and BMO valued the same weekend. Parity check: TSX TD.TO C$168.07 x 0.7019 = US$117.97 vs NYSE TD US$117.88 (0.08% gap); one NYSE share = one TSX common share. Flows, cost of equity and the equity bridge are CAD; the unsuffixed per-share values are converted to USD for comparison with the NYSE quote and the *_cad twins carry the CAD values.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, NYSE TD)
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close (Friday 2026-10-02), not an after-hours print; 52-week range 77.95-125.47 USD (TSX 109.50-175.33 CAD).
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,638.4M common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (Q3-26 Report to Shareholders Table 1, line 307; 1,638,511 thousand at line 1837) + 6.2M stock options potentially exercisable (line 3971) = 1,644.6M fully diluted. Held FLAT: equity-settled SBC is charged in the flows and buybacks are a use of the FCFE being valued, so shrinking the count as well would double-count them. Buybacks SINCE the balance-sheet date are therefore not reflected either: the C$7B NCIB completed 2026-09-25 (47.2M shares in total, part of it after 31 July) and the new up-to-C$10B / 61M-share NCIB to July 2027 (announced 2026-09-30, subject to OSFI approval) are the distribution of the FCFE, not an extra per-share lift. buyback_cash is the Q3-26 quarter's C$2,394M (9M-FY26 C$7,445M; Q3-26 cash flow statement line 3042).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CAD, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE. Canada 10y ~3.4% + beta ~1.05-1.10 x 5.75% ERP = ~9.4-9.7%. Base 9.75% -- 25bp above RY (9.5%, valued the same weekend) and equal to BMO (9.75%): TD's franchise ROE is lower (adjusted ROE 12.9% FY25, 14.8% 9M-FY26 vs RY ~17-18%), a third of the group is a US bank under a criminal plea, an asset cap and a monitorship whose timeline is not in TD's control, and the Canadian FINTRAC review is open. Bull 9.5%; bear 10.25% (only +50bp because the bear credit and remediation paths already carry most of the downside -- charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- bank; premises and lease cost (IFRS 16 depreciation and interest, lease repayments C$1,683M FY25 incl. a lease buyout) are inside non-interest expense / financing, no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Preferred dividends and distributions on other equity instruments (LRCN/AT1) -- TTM C$588M = FY25 565 less 9M-FY25 374 plus 9M-FY26 397 -- are removed INSIDE the flow as a pre-tax equivalent (588 / (1 - 0.212) = C$746M), so the after-tax flow is adjusted net income available to COMMON shareholders (TTM 16,372). Preferred shares and other equity instruments (C$12,829M at 2026-07-31; Q3-26 line 1861) are therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (RY/BMO/USB precedent; doing both charges them twice). TD has no material non-controlling interest line in the income statement.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent RY and BMO valued 2026-10-04, plus NAB.AX, HBAN, STT, NTRS, TFC, USB, WFC; SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book -- FCFE-at-CoE with retention = growth x regulatory capital is the equivalent flow form and keeps TD comparable with RY, which was valued on the same mechanics, the same CADUSD rate and the same NYSE-quote convention). No prior TD valuation and no memory entry: first build. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = adjusted total revenue (net interest income + non-interest income, gross of insurance service expenses); 'ebitda' = adjusted pre-tax income + equity-settled SBC - pre-tax-equivalent(pref/AT1 distributions); D&A 0; 'capex' = capital retention needed to hold CET1 at a 13.0% run-rate as RWA grows with revenue = CET1/revenue 1.2945 x g/(1+g); wc 0; net_debt 0 (deposits C$1.26T, wholesale funding and the NVCC subordinated debentures are operating funding / regulatory capital, not acquisition debt). TTM BUILD (adjusted, C$M; Q4-FY25 = FY25 adjusted (Annual MD&A Table 3, TD_Annual_FY2025_MDA.txt:479-491) less 9M-FY25 adjusted (Q3-26 Table 3, TD_Quarterly_Q3-FY2026.txt:491-504)): revenue 16,028 + 49,592 = 65,620 (9M-FY26 +8.3% YoY); PCL 982 + 2,957 = 3,939 (6.0% of revenue, 0.40% of average loans vs FY26 guidance 40-50bp and FY25 0.47%); insurance service expenses 1,602 + 4,666 = 6,268 (9.6% of revenue); adjusted NIE 8,540 + 25,343 = 33,883 (adjusted efficiency net of ISE 57.1%; Q4-25 8,540 ties to the MD&A quarterly text); adjusted pre-tax 4,904 + 16,626 = 21,530 (ties: 65,620 - 3,939 - 6,268 - 33,883); adjusted tax 999 + 3,571 = 4,570 (21.2%); share of Schwab income 0 (sold 2025-02-12; the 9M-FY25 C$340M adjusted equity income falls out of the TTM); adjusted NI 3,905 + 13,055 = 16,960; adjusted NI to common 3,714 + 12,658 = 16,372. ADJUSTED, NOT REPORTED: reported FY25 NI C$20,538M carries the C$8,975M pre-tax / C$8.6B net Schwab gain, C$2.8B of balance-sheet-restructuring bond losses, C$686M restructuring and C$205M of FHN hedge unwind; reported TTM NI 12,185 (20,538 - 17,258 + 12,909) is still depressed by the FY26 restructuring charges and the C$197M strategic-cards partnership charge while carrying a C$288M Schwab tax benefit. The adjusted series removes all of these; the items that remain inside adjusted earnings and ARE charged in the flow are the ~US$550M (~C$750M, 1.1% of revenue) FY26 BSA/AML remediation and governance spend, monitorship and lookback costs, and the NII drag of the asset-cap balance-sheet actions. Amortisation of acquired intangibles (C$136M pre-tax FY25) is the only non-cash adjusting item and goodwill (18,981) and intangibles are already deducted from CET1. ebitda = 21,530 + 30 - 746 = 20,814 = 31.7% of revenue. CET1: 14.3% x RWA 653.4B = C$93.4B at 2026-07-31; the 13.0% run-rate (C$84.9B = 1.2945x TTM revenue) is management's FY2026 target floor ('13%+') and the level the C$10B NCIB is deploying toward; the ~130bp (~C$8.5B, ~C$5.2/share CAD, ~US$3.6/share) held above the run-rate is NOT credited in the bridge, following the RY/BMO precedent and because OSFI, the OCC consent order (Board certification required for US-subsidiary dividends) and a possible further 7% mandated US asset reduction can all pin capital inside the group. last_fcf 12,327 = adjusted NI to common 16,372 less retention at the base year-1 growth of 5% (1.2945 x 0.05/1.05 x 65,620 = 4,045) -- an FCFE proxy; bank OCF (C$-69.6B FY25, +C$17.0B 9M-FY26) is balance-sheet noise, not owner cash. ASSET CAP: US Bank combined assets US$382B vs the US$434B cap at Oct-2025 leaves ~US$52B of headroom, so US Banking can grow inside the cap in the base case; the cap's lift (after SAR lookback completion in calendar 2027 and regulator/DOJ validation, realistically 2028+) is a bull-case catalyst, and its extension or a mandated 7% reduction is the bear case. FX: ~40% of earnings are USD-denominated (US Banking, half of Wholesale), which partly hedges the CAD->USD conversion.

bear.margin_rationale: Two legs, both disclosed risks. (1) Remediation: additional findings expand the SAR lookback, the timeline extends past calendar 2027, the asset cap persists into 2029+ and the OCC exercises the further 7% mandated US asset reduction; remediation spend stays ~C$750M+/yr and the FY2029 efficiency target slips (efficiency net of ISE 57.5% Y1, 60% Y2, 59% Y3, 58% Y4, 57.5% thereafter -- never better than today). (2) Macro: a failed CUSMA review / broad US tariffs tip Canada into recession in year 2 with unemployment past 8%; PCL rises to ~0.80% of loans (~C$8.0B, 12.2% of revenue -- FY2020 COVID was 0.69% on TD's book) in Y2, 9.0% in Y3, 7.2% in Y4 and 7.0% thereafter (~0.47%) as mortgage renewals and US CRE keep losses elevated; revenue falls 2% in Y2 (fee cycle turns, NIM compresses on BoC cuts) and recovers 1%. Pre-tax 32.0 / 24.0 / 28.1 / 30.8 / 31.5 less ~1.1% pref = 30.9 / 22.9 / 27.0 / 29.7 / 30.4. No solvency or funding case (CET1 14.3%, TLAC 31.1%, leverage 4.5%), but earnings power resets below today's 31.7% and the market re-rates TD to a discounted Big Six multiple (10x FCFE).
bear.capex_rationale: Same CET1/revenue 1.2945 x g/(1+g) formula; floor of 2.0% of revenue in the recession and recovery years (Y2-Y3) because credit migration inflates RWA even as revenue shrinks.

base.growth_rationale: 9M-FY26 adjusted revenue +8.3% YoY on record Wholesale (+25%) and Wealth (AUM +23%) quarters, FX translation and the balance-sheet repositioning NII benefit (US$500-550M). Year 1 (FY2027) steps down to 5%: Canadian P&C loan growth 3-5%, US Banking growing inside the ~US$52B of cap headroom but with the US$280M FY26 NII drag from exited portfolios still annualising, Wealth/Wholesale normalising from record fee quarters. Tapers to 3% nominal by year 10. Below the 7-10% FY2029 EPS objective because that objective also carries the buyback.
base.margin_rationale: FY0 31.7% = adjusted pre-tax 32.8% + SBC 0.05% - pref/AT1 1.1%. Components as % of gross revenue: insurance service expenses held at 9.5%; PCL normalises from 6.0% (0.40% of loans) to 6.7% (~0.45%, inside the 40-50bp guidance) by year 3; adjusted efficiency net of ISE improves 57.1% -> 56.5% (Y1) -> 56.0% -> 55.5% (Y3 = FY2029, management's 'mid-50s') -> 55.0% (Y4) and holds, which is roughly the Investor Day plan (C$825M restructuring programme completing, US$550M remediation spend fading after the calendar-2027 lookback, branch-format and AI productivity). Pre-tax 33.1 / 33.2 / 33.6 / 34.0 less ~1.0% pref = 32.0 / 32.2 / 32.5 / 32.8. Implied adjusted NI to common ~C$17.3B in year 1 (ROE ~15% on ~C$114B average common equity, vs 14.8% 9M-FY26 actual and the 13% FY26 target) rising to ~C$20B by year 4 (~16-17% ROE, the FY2029 objective met on a buyback-shrunk equity base, not beaten).
base.capex_rationale: Retention = CET1/revenue 1.2945 x g/(1+g): keeps CET1 at 13.0% as RWA grows with revenue (RWA 653.4B at 2026-07-31; 13.0% = C$84.9B). The asset cap means US RWA grows slower than revenue for the next 2-3 years, so this slightly overstates retention -- a deliberate conservatism.

bull.margin_rationale: Asset cap lifted in 2028 after a clean lookback and monitor validation; the ~C$750M/yr remediation spend falls away, the restructuring programme delivers in full and AI productivity takes adjusted efficiency net of ISE to 55.5% (Y1) / 54% / 53% / 52.5% while PCL stays benign at ~0.38% of loans (5.7-6.0% of revenue) and ISE 9.5%: pre-tax 34.3 / 35.8 / 36.8 / 37.2 less ~1.0% pref = 33.3 / 34.8 / 35.8 / 36.2. Implied ROE ~19-20%, i.e. TD closes the gap to RY.
bull.capex_rationale: Same CET1/revenue 1.2945 x g/(1+g) formula at the bull growth path; US loan growth resumes once the cap lifts, so RWA grows with revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 30/50/20 rather than the 25/50/25 used for RY and BMO the same weekend. Bear is raised to 30% because TD carries the same CUSMA/tariff macro binary as the other Canadian banks PLUS an idiosyncratic regulatory leg whose timing is explicitly 'not entirely within the Bank's control' (monitor, OCC, FRB, DOJ validation; a possible 7% mandated US asset reduction; an open FINTRAC review in Canada), and management has already had to raise the FY26 remediation cost guide once (US$500M -> US$550M). Base 50%: 9M-FY26 adjusted ROE 14.8% and Q3 16.0% are ahead of the 13% FY26 target, efficiency is already 55.2% in Q3, and management says it is ahead of the vast majority of Investor Day targets. Bull cut to 20%: the one-year TSR of 72% and ~17x TTM adjusted P/E / ~2.4x book already discount much of the recovery, and the asset-cap lift the bull needs is a 2028+ event that regulators, not TD, decide.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
